body:
The Dioxus 0.7 bridge now renders into a crate-private mutation buffer (MutationBuffer, new module mutation_buffer) with the document unborrowed, then replays it through one MutationWriter under one borrow; DioxusDocument::initial_build and Document::poll keep their signatures.
Retired: the RefCell already borrowed panic of a MountedData call (set_focus, get_client_rect, scroll_to, scroll, get_scroll_offset, get_scroll_size) in a task polled during render, on every Dioxus document; ported from upstream 286874cc1, the Dioxus 0.8 move still waiting.
The probe's two should_panic pins became mounted_data_in_a_task_a_key_handler_spawned_acts_non_incremental and _incremental (helper spawned_focus_acts, in place of press_with_spawned_focus): after the spawned task's set_focus, the engine focus, the snapshot's one focused node and the accessibility tree's focus all name focus-target, in both layout modes; the probe keeps 10 tests.
Measured: upstream's ported test task_polled_during_render_can_access_document passes with the borrow restored, so on Dioxus 0.7 it is not the fix's witness; the probe's two pins are (they fail under that mutation). Limit by construction: a task polled during render sees the document as the previous render left it.
Wrap directive: every site naming residual res-llkgqygv or res-wvatzhpe as an open owner is re-said to its row status, re-carried at 0.3.0 (target: next); a citation of line 24 of the retired residuals file goes.

Any statement that a Dioxus app's component body or a task it polls cannot safely reach the document through MountedData (focus, rect, scroll) during render: that is now allowed on every Dioxus document, the stand and the windowed dioxus-native launch included.

Any claim that upstream's task_polled_during_render_can_access_document is the witness of the buffered render, or that it is absent: it is ported and passing, but insensitive to the borrow on Dioxus 0.7; the probe's two pins are the discriminating witness there.

Focus-agreement test inventory: the probe's two pins now assert engine focus (harness.focused), the snapshot's focused node and Document::accessibility_tree focus agreeing on focus-target after a programmatic set_focus from a spawned task — a fact any section listing where the three focus readings are asserted to agree may need to carry.

body_fields.fact: A task polled during a Dioxus render acts on the document as the previous render left it, so MountedData::set_focus on a node created in the same render does not focus it (set_focus_to returns false); the probe's pins act on nodes mounted by an earlier render; the limit is recorded as an open residual row (target: next).

body:
The Dioxus 0.7 bridge now renders into a crate-private mutation buffer with the document unborrowed, then takes one borrow, replays into one MutationWriter and flushes once; ported from upstream 286874cc1 (blitz PR 1260) onto Dioxus 0.7.
This closes the MountedData hazard: a task polled during render can call set_focus, get_client_rect, scroll_to, scroll, get_scroll_offset or get_scroll_size with no RefCell already borrowed panic, on every Dioxus document.
dioxus-native-dom gains the private module mutation_buffer; the dioxus_runtime_probe's two should_panic pins become two passing tests asserting the spawned task's focus acts; upstream's task_polled_during_render_can_access_document is ported.
Measured: upstream's ported test passes even with the borrowed render restored, so on Dioxus 0.7 it is insensitive to the borrow; the probe's two pins are the fix's discriminating witness.
No dependency, manifest, lock, CI step, leg, schema or master spec moved; CI#42371051720 green 17/17; dioxus-native-dom unit tests 82 to 83, coverage 2937/3387 = 86.71 %.
The wrap also re-says owner sites naming non-open residuals to their row status: res-llkgqygv re-carried at 0.3.0 (target next); res-3v42legm and res-6ssktw6x absorbed into v030-03, owned through the CARRY cry-mjwr45xr on Upstream sync ahead of determinism and exploration.

Established Decisions, the MountedData hazard record (fct-apdputpm): it states the hazard as standing, pinned by two should_panic tests, its fix owned by the route entry MountedData buffered render. Now closed: fixed by the buffered render on the 0.7 bridge, an engine change for every Dioxus document (the stand, the windowed dioxus-native launch, any app on the bridge), flagged not upstreamable (upstream holds it in 0.8 form), nothing sent, its merge surface the bridge document file (two render sites, the field, the ported test), the new buffer module and one mod line in the crate root.

Any architecture row (hazard 3, buffer 2, title 2 rows) that names MountedData buffered render as the owner of a pending fix or says a MountedData call in a task polled inside render_immediate panics with RefCell already borrowed: that panic path is retired.
Existing Scopes, dioxus-native-dom's module list (fct-kaaobbkf): gains the private module mutation_buffer, outside every accessibility cfg gate, no pub use; keyboard_compat stays.

Existing Scopes, the dioxus_runtime_probe record (fct-ktfizprz, and probe rows naming the pins): the two should_panic pins mounted_data_in_a_task_a_key_handler_spawned_panics_non_incremental and _incremental and their helper press_with_spawned_focus are retired; they are now mounted_data_in_a_task_a_key_handler_spawned_acts_non_incremental and _incremental via the track_caller helper spawned_focus_acts, asserting presses reads 1, the harness focus, the snapshot's one focused node and the accessibility tree focus all name focus-target; the file keeps 10 tests and 0 should_panic.

Project Intent (fct-4ncs7geh) and other dioxus-08 rows that say 286874cc1 is to be ported: its buffered render is now ported onto Dioxus 0.7; the Dioxus 0.8 move itself still waits, Dioxus stays 0.7.3.
Rows that say Cells calls its MountedData handles (scroll_to) synchronously because of the hazard: the calls stay synchronous and are kept, but are no longer needed for the hazard.

Standard Contracts, Dioxus DOM bridge: DioxusDocument::initial_build and Document::poll for DioxusDocument keep their public signatures but now render through the buffer with the document unborrowed, then borrow the inner document once, build one MutationWriter, replay, drop it (the mutator's single flush), then flush queued mounted events; callers Harness::from_vdom and DioxusNativeApplication::can_create_surfaces unchanged.

Upstream's mounted-event test element_removed_before_its_mounted_event_is_flushed: any architecture row saying it returns with 286874cc1 is wrong; it stays out on Dioxus 0.7 for 0.7's scheduling, not the borrow, and returns with the Dioxus 0.8 move, owned by residual res-6ssktw6x (absorbed into v030-03) through the CARRY cry-mjwr45xr.

Architecture owner site fct-ivrm3he5 names res-llkgqygv (the stand's platform accessibility adapter and windowed AT witness) as an open owner: now re-said as owned by residual res-llkgqygv, re-carried at 0.3.0 (target next).

Architecture owner sites fct-2fe67avo, fct-hff77mh6 and fct-j4ls6r2g name res-3v42legm (merge surfaces) or res-6ssktw6x (left-out upstream delta) as open owners: each now reads absorbed into v030-03, its re-read owned by the open CARRY cry-mjwr45xr on Upstream sync ahead of determinism and exploration; this chunk's merge-surface line goes on that CARRY.

Indirect: conventions on unsafe and borrowing and the cross-cutting Rc RefCell service wiring: the bridge's borrow conflict is now avoided by recording mutations and replaying them under one borrow, a new borrow-workaround shape beside taking a child list or layout out.
Any architecture count of dioxus-native-dom's unit tests (82 in nine files) moves to 83 in nine files; the new module holds no test.

body_fields.fact: dioxus-native-dom's crate-private MutationBuffer records each of dioxus-core 0.7.10's 15 WriteMutations calls as one entry, attribute values cloned and the two texts copied into one String arena as Range<usize> spans read back by get().unwrap_or_default() with no slicing panic path; its Debug prints len alone; pub(crate) replay drains the entries in order into any WriteMutations and clears the arena keeping both allocations.

DioxusDocument holds a pub(crate) buffered_mutations MutationBuffer, set in DioxusDocument::new, its only constructor; vdom.rebuild and vdom.render_immediate write into it, never into the borrowed document.

Limit by construction of the buffered render: a task polled during render acts on the document as the previous render left it, so a node created in the same render is not yet there and set_focus_to returns false for it; recorded as an open residual row (target next).

On dioxus-core 0.7.10 a task spawned from a component body during render_immediate's RerunScope arm is first polled by the next poll's wait_for_work before the bridge borrows, while a task spawned from an event handler that also dirties a scope is first polled inside render_immediate's PollTask arm, the only path that met the borrow hazard.

Upstream's task_polled_during_render_can_access_document is ported into dioxus-native-dom's DioxusDocument tests as upstream wrote it and passes, but on Dioxus 0.7 it also passes with the borrowed render restored (insensitive to the borrow); the fix's discriminating witness on 0.7 is the dioxus_runtime_probe's two spawned_acts tests, which fail with RefCell already borrowed under that mutation.

body:
The Dioxus 0.7 bridge in dioxus-native-dom now renders into a crate-private mutation buffer while the document is unborrowed, then replays it into the document through one MutationWriter, under one borrow, in recorded order.
This holds for every Dioxus document: the stand, the windowed dioxus-native launch and any app on the bridge. A component body or a task polled during render can call MountedData set_focus, get_client_rect, scroll_to, scroll, get_scroll_offset and get_scroll_size without the RefCell already borrowed panic. That panic is retired.
Limit: a task polled during render sees the document as the previous render left it, so a node created in the same render is not yet reachable.
The probe's two should_panic pins became two tests that assert the spawned set_focus acts. The engine focus, the snapshot's one focused node and the accessibility tree's focus agree, in both layout modes.
Measured: dioxus-native-dom has 83 unit tests (was 82) and 86.71 percent coverage. CI#42371051720 was green 17/17. The stand still reads 237 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored. Upstream's ported test passes but does not detect the borrow bug on Dioxus 0.7.
No dependency, manifest, token, stylesheet, CSS default or UI element changed; Dioxus stays 0.7.3 and Cells keeps its synchronous scroll_to handles.

Any desktop-native stack or launch statement that describes how a Dioxus app opened through dioxus_native::launch renders into the document. Initial build and each poll now render through a buffer, then replay under one borrow. Public signatures are unchanged.

Any statement about programmatic scroll or into-view scroll requested through MountedData (scroll_to, scroll) that assumes it is called synchronously from a handler. It may now also be called from a task polled during render. It acts on the previous render's nodes. The scroll behaviour itself is unchanged.

Any surface or component-pattern note on focus moved by MountedData set_focus, for example a custom widget or a Dioxus app focusing an element. The call now succeeds from a task a key handler spawned. It returns false for a node created in the same render.

Any recorded hazard, caveat or should_panic pin about MountedData calls panicking during render, on any surface that runs on the Dioxus bridge. The hazard is closed, and the pins now assert that the focus acts.

Indirect: the mobile-native and web-spa surfaces run the browser app and dioxus-native on the same bridge. Any line there about the Dioxus render path or MountedData limits is reached through the bridge change.

Any citation of dioxus-native-dom line numbers in dioxus_document.rs (field near 90, constructor 155, initial_build 166-171, poll 302-307, tests after 846) may have moved. So may a statement of that crate's module list, which now holds the private mutation_buffer module beside keyboard_compat.
Any test inventory or count that cites dioxus-native-dom unit tests (82 to 83) or the dioxus_runtime_probe test names. The probe still holds 10 tests.

body_fields.fact: On a Dioxus app (desktop-native dioxus_native::launch and every other dioxus-native surface), user code that runs during a render, such as a component body or a task it polls, can call MountedData set_focus, scroll_to, scroll and the rect and scroll queries without panicking. The call acts on the document as the previous render left it, so a node created in that same render is not yet reachable and set_focus_to returns false for it.

body:
The Dioxus 0.7 bridge in dioxus-native-dom now renders into a new crate-private mutation buffer (MutationBuffer, private module mutation_buffer) with the document unborrowed, then replays it through one MutationWriter under a single borrow; DioxusDocument gains the crate-private field buffered_mutations.
This retires the RefCell already borrowed panic of a MountedData call (set_focus, get_client_rect, scroll_to and the rest) from a task polled during render_immediate, on every Dioxus document; ported from upstream 286874cc1, Dioxus 0.8 move still waiting.
The probe dioxus_runtime_probe's two should_panic pins became mounted_data_in_a_task_a_key_handler_spawned_acts_non_incremental and _incremental (helper spawned_focus_acts), the file keeping 10 tests; upstream's task_polled_during_render_can_access_document was ported and measured insensitive to the borrow on Dioxus 0.7.
Obs measurement: the buffer module and the added bridge lines hold no log site, print, env read, listener or panic token (silence gates read 0); the replay re-fires MutationWriter's own trace! calls, so the log stream is the one the direct write gave; MutationBuffer's Debug prints len alone.
No dependency, feature, manifest, CI step, harness leg, telemetry crate or driver span moved; dioxus-native-dom unit tests 82 to 83; its coverage 2937/3387 = 86.71 % at CI#42371051720 (green 17/17).

Log coverage silence records: a new dioxus-native-dom render-path module (the mutation buffer) is added with no log site, print, env read, listener or panic token; a group recording silent modules and checks must carry it.

Log coverage of dioxus-native-dom's emitters: the bridge now writes mutations through a buffer and replays them; the replay re-fires MutationWriter's existing trace! calls unchanged, so any statement about where dioxus-native-dom's debug lines fire (during render vs after) is re-read, the line set unchanged.

PII: the buffer holds element ids, tag and attribute names, attribute values and text node contents in process memory only, between render and replay; its Debug prints a length alone; nothing logs, fields or prints its contents. A pii group stating dioxus-native's logged text-node contents and attribute values may need the in-process holding added.

Any obs row on the dioxus_runtime_probe check (its silence row, its MountedData hazard, its should_panic pins, its 10-test count): the hazard is closed and the two pins are renamed and inverted to assert the spawned task's set_focus acts; the silence census over the probe still reads 0 and the 10-test count stands.

Any obs row stating a panic path in a task polled during render (RefCell already borrowed reaching escher-telemetry's panic hook or std's stderr print): that panic path is retired on every Dioxus document.

Any obs row listing dioxus-native-dom's modules or its private modules (keyboard_compat and the rest): mutation_buffer is added, private, outside every accessibility cfg gate, no pub use; keyboard_compat stays.

CI integration readings: CI#42371051720 at e26f1a207 green 17/17; per-OS tallies linux 220 · 1310 · 0 · 12, macos and coverage 201 · 1307 · 0 · 12, windows 201 · 1259 · 0 · 9, a11y 14 · 114 · 0 · 0, stand repeat 228 · 1155 · 0 · 21; any obs row citing a dated CI run's tallies stays true as dated, a current-reading row moves.
dioxus-native-dom's coverage figure, where an obs row cites it: 2937/3387 = 86.71 % (floor 83 %) at CI#42371051720; the coverage artifact upload itself is unchanged.

Upstream-sync rows: 286874cc1's buffered render is now ported onto Dioxus 0.7, its Dioxus 0.8 form and the 0.8 move still waiting; upstream's mounted-event test stays out on 0.7; a row saying 286874cc1 is still to be ported is stale.

Residual owner lines naming res-3v42legm or res-6ssktw6x (or res-fzitzzw2, opt-in OTel export) as open owners: each row reads absorbed into v030-03 (the first two) or re-carried at 0.3.0, target next (res-fzitzzw2); a site naming one with no status is re-said to its row's status.

body:
The chunk MountedData buffered render ported upstream 286874cc1's buffered render onto the Dioxus 0.7 bridge: DioxusDocument::initial_build and Document::poll now render into a crate-private MutationBuffer with the document unborrowed, then take one borrow_mut, replay through one MutationWriter and flush mounted events unchanged.
It retired the RefCell already borrowed panic of a MountedData call (set_focus, get_client_rect, scroll_to, scroll, get_scroll_offset, get_scroll_size) in a task polled inside render_immediate, on every Dioxus document; an engine change, flagged not upstreamable, nothing sent.
The probe's two should_panic pins became mounted_data_in_a_task_a_key_handler_spawned_acts_non_incremental and _incremental (helper spawned_focus_acts), asserting the spawned task's set_focus acts; the probe keeps 10 tests and no should_panic.
Measured: upstream's ported test task_polled_during_render_can_access_document passes but is insensitive to the borrow on Dioxus 0.7 (dioxus-core 0.7.10 scheduling); the two probe pins are the fix's discriminating witness (they fail with the borrowed render restored).
No dependency, manifest, lock, deny.toml, schema, config, CI step or leg moved; dioxus-native-dom unit tests 82 to 83; CI#42371051720 green 17/17.
At the wrap resume the operator directed residual owner sites re-said to their rows' status, and the stated limit recorded as an open residual row (target next).

Error Handling's record of the spawned-task MountedData panic path (stated as standing, pinned by two should_panic tests, its fix owned by the route entry MountedData buffered render) is now closed: the RefCell already borrowed panic is removed on every Dioxus document by the buffered render; the mutation control shows it returns without the fix.

Any security-plan text naming the probe's hazard pins mounted_data_in_a_task_a_key_handler_spawned_panics_non_incremental / _incremental or their helper press_with_spawned_focus: renamed and inverted to mounted_data_in_a_task_a_key_handler_spawned_acts_non_incremental / _incremental with the track_caller helper spawned_focus_acts; 0 should_panic remain and the probe file still holds 10 tests.

Any text calling upstream's task_polled_during_render_can_access_document the witness of the fix: on Dioxus 0.7 it is ported as upstream wrote it, passes, and is insensitive to the borrow; the fix's witness on 0.7 is the probe's two spawned_acts pins.

Any text stating upstream 286874cc1 is still to be ported: its buffered render is now ported onto 0.7; the Dioxus 0.8 move (0.8.0-alpha.3) is still not taken, and keyboard_compat.rs's retirement still waits on it.

Graceful degradation's try_doc returning None when the document is mutably borrowed, and MountedError::OperationFailed for missing nodes: re-read, unchanged; a render no longer holds the borrow while user code runs, so a task polled during render now reaches the document instead of meeting the borrow.

The mounted-event skip (upstream's element_removed_before_its_mounted_event_is_flushed left out, reading 1 mounted event on 0.7 where it asserts 0): still true; it stays out for Dioxus 0.7's scheduling, not the borrow, and returns with the Dioxus 0.8 move, owned by residual res-6ssktw6x (absorbed into v030-03) through the open CARRY cry-mjwr45xr on Upstream sync ahead of determinism and exploration.

Owner sites naming residual res-llkgqygv (the stand's platform accessibility adapter and its windowed AT witness, security-plan fct-agnqdsgq, fct-d2yejoup, fct-q2xi4t6k) with no status: each re-said as owned by residual res-llkgqygv, re-carried at 0.3.0 (target next).

Line citations into packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs move: 52 lines added in 8 ranges (7, 90-91, 155, 166-168, 171, 302-304, 307, 846-885); citations into events.rs and mutation_writer.rs (try_element_to_node_id, element_to_node_id at 41-49) are unmoved, mutation_writer.rs byte-identical.

Panic-path inventory for Dioxus nodes and the no-panic rule: the new module adds no unwrap, expect or panic!, and no slicing panic path (spans read by strings.get(span).unwrap_or_default()); the Dioxus nodes panic paths (event-data downcast unwraps, NodeHandle::node panics, element_to_node_id unwrap) stand unchanged.

Dioxus mutations input validation (data-dioxus-id parse, unsupported attribute values ignored, falsy booleans removed, dangerous_inner_html via set_inner_html): the mutations are now recorded and replayed in order through the same MutationWriter, so these rules hold unchanged; the buffer clones attribute values and copies text into one arena, in process only.

The engine-change record for every Dioxus document (the stand, the windowed dioxus-native launch, any app on the bridge): user code a render runs reaches the document through MountedData with no borrow panic; its merge surface (the two render sites, the field, the ported test, the new module, one mod line) is re-read at the next upstream sync under res-3v42legm, absorbed into v030-03, owned by the CARRY cry-mjwr45xr.

The limit by construction: a task polled during render acts on the document as the previous render left it, so set_focus_to returns false for a node created in the same render; recorded as an open residual row (target next).

Per-OS CI tallies dated at CI#41333172440: true as dated; the new reading is CI#42371051720 at e26f1a207, green 17/17 (linux 220 result lines, 1310 passed, 0 failed, 12 ignored); the stand 237 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored over 51 files, unchanged.
Dependency statements for the Dioxus bridge: unchanged and re-read; Dioxus stays 0.7.3 with dioxus-core 0.7.10 in the lock, no package entered or left, and the audit leg green.

body_fields.fact: dioxus-native-dom's crate-private MutationBuffer (its render-path recorder) holds no unwrap, expect or panic!, and reads each recorded text span by strings.get(span).unwrap_or_default(), so it has no slicing panic path; its spans are Range<usize> into one arena, needing no u32::try_from(...).expect(...).

initial_build and poll on DioxusDocument render into the MutationBuffer with the document unborrowed, then take one borrow_mut, replay through one MutationWriter, drop the borrow and flush mounted events; a task polled during render that calls MountedData acts on the document as the previous render left it, so set_focus_to returns false for a node created in that same render, an open residual (target next).

dioxus-native-dom's MutationBuffer adds no log site, print, env read or listener; its Debug prints len alone, it holds ids, tag and attribute names, attribute values and text in process only, and its replay re-fires MutationWriter's own trace! calls, so the log stream is the one the direct write gave.

body:
The session ported upstream 286874cc1's buffered render onto the Dioxus 0.7 bridge: dioxus-native-dom gains the crate-private module mutation_buffer (MutationBuffer, recording dioxus-core 0.7.10's 15 WriteMutations calls), and DioxusDocument::initial_build and Document::poll render into it with the document unborrowed, then replay it through one MutationWriter.
It retired the RefCell already borrowed panic of a MountedData call in a task polled inside render_immediate, on every Dioxus document, and turned the probe's two should_panic pins into mounted_data_in_a_task_a_key_handler_spawned_acts_non_incremental and _incremental over the helper spawned_focus_acts, which assert the engine focus, the snapshot's one focused node and the accessibility tree focus all name focus-target.
It ported upstream's task_polled_during_render_can_access_document unit test, and a mutation control measured it insensitive to the borrow on Dioxus 0.7 (ok with the borrowed render restored, while the two pins read FAILED); on the operator's ruling the specs are amended so the probe's two pins are the fix's witness on 0.7.
It measured dioxus-native-dom at 83 unit tests (82 before), its coverage at 2937/3387 = 86.71 % on CI#42371051720 (green 17/17), and re-read the per-OS CI tallies there; no dependency, gate, leg or harness surface moved.
Its wrap addendum re-says the residual owners res-llkgqygv (re-carried at 0.3.0, target next) and res-3v42legm and res-6ssktw6x (absorbed into v030-03, re-read through the CARRY cry-mjwr45xr on Upstream sync ahead of determinism and exploration).

The witness record (fct-e2zfwpza) calls upstream's task_polled_during_render_can_access_document the witness of the route entry MountedData buffered render; measured false on Dioxus 0.7: the test is now ported (dioxus_document.rs 846-885, fn at 850), passes and is insensitive to the borrow on 0.7, guarding the 0.8 scheduling; the fix's discriminating witness on 0.7 is the probe's two spawned_acts pins.
dioxus-native-dom's unit count (fct-i5a6vv3t): 82 unit tests in nine files becomes 83 in nine files; the new mutation_buffer module holds no test.

The MountedData hazard records (fct-kgita7a3 in E2E, and any scope or CI row stating the hazard standing, pinned by two should_panic tests, its fix owned by the route entry MountedData buffered render): the hazard is now closed, fixed by the buffered render on the 0.7 bridge.

The probe's pins (fct-mealwlke, fct-luwk6iun, fct-o7txuegv and every row naming mounted_data_in_a_task_a_key_handler_spawned_panics_non_incremental, _incremental or the helper press_with_spawned_focus): renamed and inverted to mounted_data_in_a_task_a_key_handler_spawned_acts_non_incremental and _incremental over spawned_focus_acts, which boots through hazard_ready(hazard_spawned, incremental), presses ArrowDown and asserts presses reads 1 and the engine, snapshot and tree focus name focus-target; the probe holds 0 should_panic and still 10 tests.

Upstream's mounted-event test element_removed_before_its_mounted_event_is_flushed (fct-ybmlkzsq), recorded as returning with 286874cc1: it stays out on Dioxus 0.7 for 0.7's scheduling, not the borrow, and returns with the Dioxus 0.8 move, owned by residual res-6ssktw6x (absorbed into v030-03) through the CARRY cry-mjwr45xr.
Rows saying 286874cc1 is to be ported: its buffered render is now ported; the Dioxus 0.8 move (0.8.0-alpha.3) is still not taken, and keyboard_compat.rs's retirement still waits on it.
